🏛️ Chapter 1: Sources for the History of Modern India
🎯 LEVEL 1: Book-Strict Knowledge (Questions 1 - 30)
Q1. Which material is given the utmost priority in constructing the history of modern India? (a) Creative Literature (b) Archives (c) Oral Evidence (d) Biographies
* Answer: (b) Archives
Q2. The records of the East India Company provide a detailed account of trading conditions during which specific period? (a) 1600–1757 (b) 1600–1857 (c) 1757–1857 (d) 1600–1947
Q3. Official records in India are broadly classified into how many categories? (a) Three (Central, State, Judicial) (b) Four (Central, State, Intermediate, Judicial) (c) Two (Central, State) (d) Five
* Answer: (b) Four (Central, State, Intermediate, Judicial)
Q4. Where are the archives of the Government of India mostly housed? (a) National Museum, New Delhi (b) National Archives of India, New Delhi (c) Asiatic Society, Kolkata (d) Parliament Library
* Answer: (b) National Archives of India, New Delhi
Q5. Who was appointed as the first Surveyor General of Bengal, and in what year? (a) James Rennell, 1767 (b) William Jones, 1784 (c) James Prinsep, 1837 (d) Thomas Munro, 1820
* Answer: (a) James Rennell, 1767
Q6. To deal with political and communal issues exclusively, which new series of records was started in 1907? (a) Home Public (b) Home Reforms (c) Home Political (d) Foreign Political
* Answer: (c) Home Political
Q7. The records of the Reforms Office are highly useful for the analytical study of constitutional developments during which period? (a) 1909–1919 (b) 1920–1937 (c) 1935–1947 (d) 1858–1909
Q8. The Khalsa Darbar records, housed in Lahore, pertain to which period? (a) 1700–1750 (b) 1800–1849 (c) 1849–1900 (d) 1750–1800
Q9. Where is the Peshwa Daftar, a valuable source for Maratha history, housed? (a) National Archives, New Delhi (b) Alienation Office, Pune (c) State Archives, Mumbai (d) Bikaner Archives
* Answer: (b) Alienation Office, Pune
Q10. The Rajasthan State Archives are located in which city? (a) Jaipur (b) Jodhpur (c) Bikaner (d) Udaipur
* Answer: (c) Bikaner
Q11. The historical records of the Dogra rule (from 1846 onwards) are housed where? (a) Srinagar (b) Jammu (c) Shimla (d) Lahore
* Answer: (b) Jammu
Q12. In which year were the early records of Fort Williams lost during the sack of Calcutta? (a) 1756 (b) 1757 (c) 1764 (d) 1793
* Answer: (a) 1756
Q13. The Madras Presidency records, which survived intact, begin from which year? (a) AD 1600 (b) AD 1639 (c) AD 1670 (d) AD 1700
* Answer: (c) AD 1670

Q14. The archives of the Bombay Presidency are primarily housed in which institution? (a) Asiatic Society of Bombay (b) Maharashtra Secretariat Record Office, Mumbai (c) Alienation Office, Pune (d) National Archives, New Delhi
* Answer: (b) Maharashtra Secretariat Record Office, Mumbai
Q15. The Portuguese archives preserved in Goa primarily belong to which period? (a) 1500–1700 (b) 1600–1800 (c) 1700–1900 (d) 1800–1961
Q16. The Dutch records regarding Cochin and Malabar are located in which record office? (a) State Archives of West Bengal (b) Madras Record Office (c) Goa Archives (d) National Archives, New Delhi
* Answer: (b) Madras Record Office
Q17. To which city were the French archives of Chandernagore and Pondicherry taken before India's independence? (a) London (b) Lisbon (c) Paris (d) Amsterdam
* Answer: (c) Paris
Q18. In which year were the Danish possessions of Tranquebar and Serampore sold to the English East India Company? (a) 1800 (b) 1845 (c) 1857 (d) 1793
* Answer: (b) 1845
Q19. The earliest available judicial archives pertain to which court? (a) Supreme Court of Bengal (b) Mayor’s Court at Fort St. George (c) Mayor’s Court at Bombay (d) High Court of Calcutta
* Answer: (b) Mayor’s Court at Fort St. George (beginning AD 1689)
Q20. What is the status of the pre-Plassey records of the Mayor’s Court at Fort Williams? (a) Housed in London (b) Housed in New Delhi (c) They have been lost (d) Housed in Kolkata
* Answer: (c) They have been lost
Q21. The archives of the Supreme Court of Bengal cover which period? (a) 1773–1857 (b) 1774–1861 (c) 1757–1858 (d) 1861–1947
Q22. Where are the papers of the Indian National Congress primarily housed? (a) National Archives of India (b) Parliament Library (c) Nehru Memorial Museum and Library, New Delhi (d) Asiatic Society
* Answer: (c) Nehru Memorial Museum and Library, New Delhi
Q23. The 'India Office Records' are an important archival group housed in which city? (a) New Delhi (b) London (c) Paris (d) Kolkata
* Answer: (b) London
Q24. Who wrote the book Hindu Manners and Customs, which provides useful information on the socio-economic life of Indians? (a) Bishop Heber (b) Abbe Dubois (c) James Burnes (d) C.J.C. Davidson
* Answer: (b) Abbe Dubois
Q25. Narrative of a Visit to the Court of Sinde was written by whom? (a) Alexander Burnes (b) James Burnes (c) John Butler (d) W.H. Sleeman
* Answer: (b) James Burnes
Q26. Who made the first unsuccessful attempt to start a newspaper in India in 1776? (a) James Augustus Hickey (b) William Bolts (c) J.S. Buckingham (d) Raja Rammohan Roy
* Answer: (b) William Bolts
Q27. What was the name of the first newspaper published in India in 1780? (a) The Calcutta Gazette (b) The Madras Courier (c) The Bengal Gazette (d) The Bombay Herald
* Answer: (c) The Bengal Gazette (or Calcutta General Advertiser)

Q28. The famous novel Anandamath (1882), which features the lyric 'Vandemataram', was written by whom? (a) Rabindranath Tagore (b) Bankim Chandra Chatterjee (c) Sarat Chandra Chatterjee (d) Dinabandhu Mitra
* Answer: (b) Bankim Chandra Chatterjee

Q29. What is the alternative name for the 'Patna Kalam' school of painting that emerged under British patronage? (a) Kalighat Paintings (b) Company Paintings (c) Tanjore Paintings (d) Pahari Paintings
* Answer: (b) Company Paintings
Q30. The painting Relief of Lucknow (1859), which commemorates British heroes of the 1857 revolt, was painted by whom? (a) Thomas Jones Barker (b) Tilly Kettle (c) William Hodges (d) George Chinnery
* Answer: (a) Thomas Jones Barker
Chapter 1: Sources for the History of Modern India
📈 LEVEL 2: Upgraded (Easy to Moderate UPSC Standard) (Integrating strict book knowledge with foundational external UPSC context for deeper conceptual clarity)
Q1. Consider the following statements regarding the National Archives of India (NAI):
1. It is the repository of the non-current records of the Government of India.
2. It was originally established in New Delhi in 1891 and remained there ever since. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? (a) 1 only (b) 2 only (c) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2
* Answer: (a) 1 only

* Explanation: While statement 1 is true (from book knowledge), statement 2 is false. The NAI was originally established as the Imperial Record Department in Calcutta in 1891, and its transfer to New Delhi was completed only in 1926 following the shift of the capital in 1911.

Q2. The records of the East India Company (EIC) are vital for the 1600–1857 period. The EIC's early trade and administration, documented in these archives, were initially legitimized by a Royal Charter granted by: (a) King James I (b) Queen Elizabeth I (c) King Charles II (d) Queen Victoria
* Answer: (b) Queen Elizabeth I
* Explanation: The EIC was formed in 1600 via a royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I, giving them a monopoly on trade in the East.

Q3. James Rennell was appointed as the first Surveyor General of Bengal in 1767 to scientifically map the region. Under whose governorship was this crucial administrative step taken? (a) Warren Hastings (b) Lord Cornwallis (c) Lord Clive (d) Lord Wellesley
* Answer: (c) Lord Clive
* Explanation: Lord Clive was serving his second term as Governor of Bengal (1765-1767) when Rennell was appointed to map the newly acquired Diwani territories of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

Q4. The 'Peshwa Daftar', a massive collection of administrative and military documents crucial for studying Maratha history, is primarily written in which script? (a) Devanagari (b) Brahmi (c) Modi (d) Kharosthi
* Answer: (c) Modi
* Explanation: The Maratha administrative records housed in the Alienation Office (Pune) were predominantly maintained in the Modi script, a cursive script used to write Marathi.

Q5. The Khalsa Darbar records in Lahore are invaluable for studying the socio-economic conditions of Punjab between 1800 and 1849. This period largely coincides with the reign and legacy of which prominent ruler? (a) Guru Gobind Singh (b) Banda Singh Bahadur (c) Maharaja Ranjit Singh (d) Dalip Singh
* Answer: (c) Maharaja Ranjit Singh
* Explanation: Maharaja Ranjit Singh consolidated the Sikh Empire beginning in 1799. He ruled until his death in 1839, and the empire fell to the British in 1849.

Q6. Portuguese records preserved in Goa are crucial for understanding the 'Estado da India'. Which of the following was the first headquarters of the Portuguese in India before it was shifted to Goa in 1530? (a) Calicut (b) Cochin (c) Cannanore (d) Diu
* Answer: (b) Cochin
* Explanation: Cochin was the first capital of the Portuguese in India. It was later shifted to Goa by Nuno da Cunha in 1530.

Q7. The archives of the French possessions (Chandernagore, Pondicherry) were moved to Paris. The French East India Company (Compagnie des Indes Orientales) was established in 1664 during the reign of which French monarch? (a) Louis XIII (b) Louis XIV (c) Louis XV (d) Louis XVI
* Answer: (b) Louis XIV
* Explanation: The company was founded by Jean-Baptiste Colbert, the finance minister to King Louis XIV.

Q8. Dutch records relating to Cochin and Malabar are preserved in Madras. The Dutch influence in the Malabar region significantly declined after their crushing defeat by the Travancore Kingdom in which famous 1741 battle? (a) Battle of Wandiwash (b) Battle of Colachel (c) Battle of Bedara (d) Battle of Swally
* Answer: (b) Battle of Colachel
* Explanation: King Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeated the Dutch East India Company at Colachel, ending their political power in Kerala.

Q9. The earliest available judicial archives relate to the Mayor’s Court at Fort St. George (Madras), beginning in 1689. What was the primary purpose of establishing the Mayor's Courts in the Presidency towns? (a) To try cases of mutiny among British soldiers. (b) To handle civil litigation primarily involving the English and Europeans. (c) To apply traditional Hindu and Islamic laws to the local populace. (d) To adjudicate international trade disputes with the French.
* Answer: (b) To handle civil litigation primarily involving the English and Europeans.
* Explanation: Mayor's courts were early Crown courts established by Royal Charter to bring English legal principles to the Company's settlements.

Q10. The private archives of the Indian National Congress (INC) are housed in the Nehru Memorial Museum. Who among the following was the key British civil servant instrumental in organizing the first session of the INC in 1885? (a) Lord Dufferin (b) Allan Octavian Hume (c) William Wedderburn (d) Lord Ripon
* Answer: (b) Allan Octavian Hume
* Explanation: A.O. Hume, a retired civil servant, played a foundational role in convening the INC.

Q11. Abbe Jean de la Serve Dubois wrote Hindu Manners and Customs. He was a French Catholic missionary who integrated himself into local society to observe customs, predominantly in which region? (a) Bengal (b) Punjab (c) Mysore / South India (d) Awadh
* Answer: (c) Mysore / South India
